recognize_zh: 箭頭指向中性球核葉旁以細柄相連的一顆小而緻密的圓形染色質突起（drumstick），即 Barr body；此中性球約有五葉，紅血球背景呈乾燥假影。
features: Segmented neutrophil with about five nuclear lobes
Small, round, dense chromatin drumstick attached to a lobe by a short thin stalk (arrow)
Red cells with variable central pallor and drying/refractile artifact; occasional crenated cells
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a neutrophil with approximately five nuclear lobes and a small, round, dense chromatin appendage attached to one lobe by a thin stalk, consistent with a drumstick. Red cells show drying artifact with irregular central pallor, and platelets are present. A single five-lobed neutrophil is not sufficient to define hypersegmentation. Findings represent a Barr body (inactive X chromosome) in a neutrophil, a normal finding in females.

ddx.vs: Hypersegmentation requires at least 6 lobes in one cell or more than 5% five-lobed neutrophils and is not defined by a small round appendage.
Nodules lack the thin filament and discrete round head that define a drumstick.
Döhle bodies are pale-blue cytoplasmic patches at the cell periphery, not dense chromatin connected to the nucleus.
